page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, translating to a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C x86_64 processor operating at 2.3 GHz, the instance is built on 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes hardware-level support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scores reaching 2228.0, placing it in the top tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong results, processing at 34.85 GB/sec and 15.13 GB/sec respectively. However, multi-threaded and memory-intensive operations show clear performance tradeoffs. The instance's multi-core stress-ng performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression are categorized as weak, and memory bandwidth is limited, with large block read and write speeds registering at 32.55 GB/sec and 20.39 GB/sec. Passmark memory scores and Redis SET operations also fall into the lower performance tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-highcpu-4 offers a specialized compute-to-memory ratio designed for workloads that prioritize single-core CPU execution over massive memory capacity or high memory bandwidth. Given the strong single-threaded performance but weaker multi-core scaling and memory throughput, this instance is suited for lightweight single-threaded processing, basic text processing, static web serving, and small-scale LLM prompt processing. It is less suitable for memory-bound databases, software compilation, or highly parallelized multi-threaded computing.
